mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which is a precursor to economic slowdown and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate activity (HOUST) reflects a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 55% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a mismatch between labor supply and demand, leading to economic inefficiencies and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.
